title: The Janis band: Central Plaza, personnel, and Elmer Schoebel
summary: Janis's band played Fridays and Saturdays at the Central Plaza and on Arthur Godfrey, with Dick Smith, Tom Sharpstein and Elmer Schoebel.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it

blocks.x: Yes. Mostly at the Central Plaza. We used to work there every Friday and Saturday night. And we used to work a few other jobs too. We did, I don't know, we were on the Arthur Godfrey Show. A lot of things like that. Who else was in the band? A guy named Dick Smith on trumpet. He was from the west coast. He was influenced by Bunk mainly. And, well, before I was in the band, there was a clarinet player named Tom Sharpstein, who used to do a very good imitation of George Lewis. And, when I was in the band, the piano player was Elmer Schoble. You know who he is. Yes, indeed.

And, he certainly was pleased with the first New Orleans men to come up because he worked with them steadily. Both at the Friars and at Midway Gardens. Although, now that I say Midway, I can't remember that there were many New Orleans. They were mainly Chicagoans. However, they were greatly influenced by the Friars where Schoble had been active. Did Schoble continue his activity in composing or arranging at that time?
Yes, I think he was trying to sell some tunes. And, I don't think he got very far with it. But, he wasn't very active otherwise.

I can't remember that there were any New Orleans pianists around New York with a possible exception. Lou Russell was out of the band business by that time. Yeah, Lou Russell died about six months ago. And, uh... No, offhand, I can't remember who the others who might have been around New York. But, if you don't recall of mine, it's not likely that we missed many of the first generation men.
